source.text: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד מִן־הָרָמָתַ֛יִם צוֹפִ֖ים מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמ֡וֹ אֶ֠לְקָנָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֧ם בֶּן־אֱלִיה֛וּא בֶּן־תֹּ֥חוּ בֶן־צ֖וּף אֶפְרָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And there was a man, one, from Ramathaim-zophim, from [the] hill country of Ephraim, and his name [was] Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

en.L: And there was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name [was] Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
en.B: There was a man from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim named Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
en.R: There was a man named Elkanah who lived in the town of Ramathaim-zophim, in the hills of Ephraim. His father was Jeroham, and his family line went back through Elihu and Tohu to Zuph. He was from Ephraim.

es.L: Y hubo cierto hombre de Ramataim-zofim, de la región montañosa de Efraín, y su nombre [era] Elcana hijo de Jeroham, hijo de Eliú, hijo de Tohu, hijo de Zuf, efraimita.
es.B: Había un hombre de Ramataim-zofim, en la región montañosa de Efraín, llamado Elcana hijo de Jeroham, hijo de Eliú, hijo de Tohu, hijo de Zuf, efraimita.
es.R: Había un hombre llamado Elcana que vivía en el pueblo de Ramataim-zofim, en las colinas de Efraín. Su padre era Jeroham, y su linaje se remontaba por Eliú y Tohu hasta Zuf. Era de Efraín.

fr.L: Et il y avait un homme, [un certain homme] de Ramathaïm-Tsophim, de la montagne d’Éphraïm, et son nom [était] Elqana, fils de Yeroham, fils d’Élihou, fils de Tohou, fils de Tsouph, un Éphraïmite.
fr.B: Il y avait un homme de Ramathaïm-Tsophim, dans la montagne d’Éphraïm, qui s’appelait Elqana, fils de Yeroham, fils d’Élihou, fils de Tohou, fils de Tsouph ; c’était un Éphraïmite.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme qui s’appelait Elqana. Il habitait la ville de Ramathaïm-Tsophim, dans les collines d’Éphraïm. Son père était Yeroham, et ses ancêtres étaient Élihou, Tohou et Tsouph. Il était de la région d’Éphraïm.

vi.L: Có một người kia từ Ra-ma-tha-im Xô-phim, thuộc miền đồi núi Ép-ra-im, tên [là] Ên-ca-na, con trai Giê-rô-ham, con trai Ê-li-hu, con trai Thô-hu, con trai Xu-phơ, người Ép-ra-im.
vi.B: Có một người ở Ra-ma-tha-im Xô-phim, thuộc miền đồi núi Ép-ra-im, tên là Ên-ca-na, con trai Giê-rô-ham, cháu Ê-li-hu, chắt Thô-hu, dòng dõi Xu-phơ, người Ép-ra-im.
vi.R: Có một người tên là Ên-ca-na sống tại thị trấn Ra-ma-tha-im Xô-phim, trong vùng đồi núi Ép-ra-im. Cha ông là Giê-rô-ham, và dòng họ ông bắt nguồn từ Ê-li-hu, Thô-hu cho đến Xu-phơ. Ông thuộc chi tộc Ép-ra-im.

decisions.choice: the setting: the last days of the judges, before Israel had a king
decisions.reason: The book opens where Judges leaves off. Israel has no king (Judges 21:25), and Eli the priest has led Israel from the sanctuary at Shiloh (verses 3 and 9; 4:18). The story of Samuel, the last of the judges (7:15), who will anoint Israel's first two kings (10:1; 16:13), begins with one ordinary family in the hills of Ephraim. 1 and 2 Samuel were a single book in the Hebrew Bible; the division into two comes from the ancient Greek translation.

decisions.choice: There was a certain man from ...: the opening of Judges 13 and 17
decisions.reason: The words echo the start of Samson's story, "There was a certain man from Zorah ... and his name was Manoah" (Judges 13:2), and of Micah's (Judges 17:1). As in Samson's story, a wife who cannot have children and a son given by God follow (verse 2).

decisions.choice: Ramathaim-zophim: "the two heights" of the Zuphites, the town called Ramah in verse 19
decisions.reason: Ramathaim means "two heights". Elsewhere the town is simply Ramah, "the height" (verse 19; 2:11), and it is Samuel's home all his life (7:17). Zophim seems to point to the family of Zuph, named at the end of the verse; the area is called "the land of Zuph" in 9:5. The letters can also be divided to read "Ramathaim, a Zuphite", describing Elkanah; the sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: Ephraimite: a man of the hill country of Ephraim
decisions.reason: The word can also mean someone from Ephrathah, the clan around Bethlehem (Ruth 1:2; 1 Samuel 17:12), but the hill country of Ephraim in this verse decides the sense here, as in Judges 12:5 and 1 Kings 11:26. It says where the family lived. 1 Chronicles 6 lists Elkanah and Samuel among the descendants of Levi, a tribe that had towns within Ephraim (Joshua 21:20-22).

decisions.choice: the town of ...; his family line went back through ... to Zuph
decisions.reason: Readable says that Ramathaim-zophim is a town and turns the list of ancestors into a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced; passé composé at Readable ("il est monté", "elle a pleuré"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level, for the whole of 1 Samuel 1-15
decisions.reason: As the French style guide and the Pentateuch note set for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. This verse only describes ("il y avait"); the narrative tenses begin in verse 3.

decisions.choice: "Ramathaïm-Tsophim", "Elqana", "Yeroham", "Élihou", "Tohou", "Tsouph"
decisions.reason: Names follow the Samuel terms note ("Elqana", with q for the Hebrew qof, as "Eqrôn" and "Qiryath-Yearim"); the other ancestors are transcribed the same way, with French "ou" for the Hebrew u and "ts" for tsade, and the diaeresis that keeps the vowels apart in "Ramathaïm", as in "Éphraïm".

decisions.choice: "Ramataim-zofim", "Elcana", "Jeroham", "Eliú", "Tohu", "Zuf", "efraimita"
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel: names follow the Samuel terms note (Elcana, Ana, Penina, Elí, Ofni, Finés, Samuel, Silo, Ramá) and otherwise their usual Spanish form, kept the same through both books. The town keeps the hyphenated form of the English; "efraimita" says what the English "Ephraimite" says (m4), where "efrateo" could suggest Ephrathah.

decisions.choice: the names in the forms "Ra-ma-tha-im Xô-phim", "Ên-ca-na", "Giê-rô-ham", "Ê-li-hu", "Thô-hu", "Xu-phơ", "Ép-ra-im"
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note gives "Ên-ca-na"; the others follow the usual Protestant transliteration, and "Ép-ra-im" is the form of the published Genesis. Kept the same through 1 and 2 Samuel.

decisions.choice: "con trai ... cháu ... chắt ... dòng dõi" for the chain of "son of"
decisions.reason: Balanced lets Vietnamese kinship words show the generations; Literal repeats "con trai" as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וְלוֹ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֔ים שֵׁ֤ם אַחַת֙ חַנָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פְּנִנָּ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י לִפְנִנָּה֙ יְלָדִ֔ים וּלְחַנָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין יְלָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And to him [were] two wives; [the] name of one [was] Hannah, and [the] name of the second [was] Peninnah. And there were to Peninnah children, and to Hannah there were no children.

en.L: And he had two wives: the name of one [was] Hannah, and the name of the second [was] Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
en.B: He had two wives. One was named Hannah and the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
en.R: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah did not have any.

es.L: Y él tenía dos esposas: el nombre de una [era] Ana, y el nombre de la segunda [era] Penina. Y Penina tenía hijos, pero Ana no tenía hijos.
es.B: Tenía dos esposas. Una se llamaba Ana y la otra Penina. Penina tenía hijos, pero Ana no tenía ninguno.
es.R: Elcana tenía dos esposas, Ana y Penina. Penina tenía hijos, pero Ana no tenía ninguno.

fr.L: Et il avait deux femmes : le nom de l’une [était] Anne, et le nom de la seconde [était] Peninna. Et Peninna avait des enfants, mais Anne n’avait pas d’enfants.
fr.B: Il avait deux femmes. L’une s’appelait Anne et l’autre Peninna. Peninna avait des enfants, mais Anne n’en avait pas.
fr.R: Elqana avait deux femmes, Anne et Peninna. Peninna avait des enfants, mais Anne n’en avait pas.

vi.L: Ông có hai vợ: tên của một người [là] An-ne, và tên của người thứ hai [là] Phê-ni-na. Phê-ni-na có con, còn An-ne không có con.
vi.B: Ông có hai vợ. Một người tên là An-ne, người kia tên là Phê-ni-na. Phê-ni-na có con, còn An-ne thì không.
vi.R: Ên-ca-na có hai vợ là An-ne và Phê-ni-na. Phê-ni-na có con, nhưng An-ne thì không có đứa con nào.

decisions.choice: two wives: a home with a rival wife
decisions.reason: The law allowed a man more than one wife (Deuteronomy 21:15-17), but Scripture's stories of such homes are stories of rivalry: Sarah and Hagar (Genesis 16), Rachel and Leah (Genesis 29:31-30:24). Peninnah will be called Hannah's rival (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Hannah had no children: a deep grief and a shame
decisions.reason: A wife without children was often pitied or looked down on (Genesis 16:4; 30:1, 23). Hannah joins the women of Scripture who could not have children until God gave them a son: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel and the wife of Manoah (Genesis 11:30; 25:21; 29:31; Judges 13:2).

decisions.choice: Hannah: "grace" or "favor"; Peninnah: perhaps "pearl" or "coral"
decisions.reason: Hannah's name comes from the word for grace or favor. Peninnah's is less certain; it may come from a word for a precious stone, pearl or coral. The story does not make anything of either meaning.

decisions.choice: the second: the other wife
decisions.reason: The word means "second". It may simply mean "the other one", or that Elkanah married Peninnah after Hannah. The text does not say why he took a second wife.

decisions.choice: Elkanah had two wives
decisions.reason: Readable names Elkanah for "he" and gives the two names in one sentence.

decisions.choice: "Anne" for Hannah
decisions.reason: French has long called Hannah "Anne", the same name as Mary's mother in Christian tradition; the Samuel terms note settles "Anne" for both books. The Hebrew sense of the name, "grace" (m3), is the same either way.

decisions.choice: "An-ne" and "Phê-ni-na"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: "An-ne" is the traditional Protestant form of Hannah, the same Hebrew name the Vietnamese Luke 2:36 gives the prophetess.

source.text: וְעָלָה֩ הָאִ֨ישׁ הַה֤וּא מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀יָמִ֔ימָה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֧ת וְלִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּשִׁלֹ֑ה וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עֵלִ֗י חָפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣נְחָ֔ס כֹּהֲנִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the man, that [one], from his city from days to days to bow down and to sacrifice to Yahweh of hosts in Shiloh; and there [were the] two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests to Yahweh.

en.L: And that man went up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts in Shiloh; and there the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, [were] priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Year after year this man went up from his town to worship and to offer sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies at Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there.
en.R: Every year Elkanah left his town and went up to Shiloh to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies and to offer sacrifices to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served as priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there.

es.L: Y aquel hombre subía de su ciudad año tras año para adorar y para ofrecer sacrificios {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los ejércitos en Silo; y allí los dos hijos de Elí, Ofni y Finés, [eran] sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Año tras año este hombre subía desde su pueblo a Silo para adorar y ofrecer sacrificios {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos. Allí eran sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} los dos hijos de Elí, Ofni y Finés.
es.R: Cada año Elcana salía de su pueblo y subía a Silo para adorar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos y ofrecerle sacrificios. Los dos hijos de Elí, Ofni y Finés, servían allí como sacerdotes {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et cet homme-là montait de sa ville d’année en année pour se prosterner et pour sacrifier {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} des armées à Silo ; et là [étaient] les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Chaque année, cet homme montait de sa ville pour adorer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées et lui offrir des sacrifices à Silo. Les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, y étaient prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Chaque année, Elqana quittait sa ville et montait à Silo pour adorer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées et pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} offrir des sacrifices. Les deux fils d’Éli, Hophni et Phinéas, étaient prêtres {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} là-bas.

vi.L: Người ấy từ thành mình đi lên hằng năm để thờ lạy và dâng sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân tại Si-lô; và ở đó hai con trai của Hê-li là Hóp-ni và Phi-nê-a [làm] thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Năm này qua năm khác, người ấy từ thành mình đi lên Si-lô để thờ phượng và dâng sinh tế cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân. Hai con trai của Hê-li là Hóp-ni và Phi-nê-a làm thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại đó.
vi.R: Mỗi năm Ên-ca-na rời thành mình đi lên Si-lô để thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân và dâng sinh tế cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Hai con trai của Hê-li là Hóp-ni và Phi-nê-a làm thầy tế lễ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở đó.

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: Yahweh, commander of the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: This is the first time the title appears in the Bible. Tseba'ot is the plural of tsava', an army or host, a great company drawn up in ranks. The word is used of Israel's armies (Exodus 12:41; 1 Samuel 17:45), of the sun, moon and stars (Genesis 2:1; Deuteronomy 4:19) and of the heavenly beings around God's throne (1 Kings 22:19). Joined to God's name, it presents Yahweh as the King who commands every power in heaven and on earth. In 1 Samuel the title is tied to the ark kept at Shiloh, "the ark of the covenant of Yahweh of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim" (4:4), and David goes out against Goliath "in the name of Yahweh of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel" (17:45). Hannah calls on God by this name in her vow (verse 11).

decisions.choice: Shiloh: the place of Israel's central sanctuary
decisions.reason: Shiloh lay in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Bethel (Judges 21:19). The tent of meeting had been set up there in Joshua's day (Joshua 18:1), and the ark of the covenant was kept there (3:3; 4:3-4). Israelites went up to it for a yearly feast (Judges 21:19).

decisions.choice: from days to days: year by year
decisions.reason: "Days" here stands for a full year, as in Exodus 13:10 and Judges 11:40; 21:19. The visit was a yearly one (verses 7 and 21), perhaps at one of the great feasts.

decisions.choice: Hophni and Phinehas: Eli's sons, the priests at Shiloh
decisions.reason: Eli was the chief priest (verse 9), and his sons served with him. The writer names them here because of what follows: they will treat Yahweh's offerings with contempt (2:12-17), and both will die on one day, as a sign against Eli's house (2:34; 4:11). Phinehas bears the name of Aaron's faithful grandson (Numbers 25:7-13).

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: "Hosts" was once the ordinary word for an army, but today it most often means someone who welcomes guests, so it hides what the title says. Balanced and Readable say "Armies", as in Isaiah and throughout Samuel and Kings: it states the meaning plainly and keeps the picture of a commander. "Almighty" was considered, but it turns the picture into an abstract quality. Literal keeps the traditional "the LORD of hosts".

decisions.choice: Year after year this man (Balanced); Every year Elkanah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time first, and Readable names Elkanah for "that man" and says that the sacrifices were offered to the LORD.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} for the divine name, at every level of both books
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note settles: the default "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals matches the English "the LORD" and the Spanish "el SEÑOR"; the reader setting gives the name itself, "Yahvé". "L’Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer. The span takes in the article and its contractions ("du SEIGNEUR", "au SEIGNEUR").

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR des armées" at every level
decisions.reason: French "armées" says plainly what the English Balanced and Readable say with "Armies" (r-en-1) and what the traditional "hosts" meant, so one wording serves all three levels, as in the published Psalms. "Tout-puissant" would turn the picture of a commander into an abstract quality, the reason the English gives against "Almighty".

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, taking in the article and its contractions ("al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé", "del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé"); in address, "{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}" with no article
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as in the Pentateuch and Psalms: the name is "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the reader setting. "Jehová" is a later hybrid form, and plain "el Señor" would hide that the name is used. Deity pronoun spans go only on words Spanish writes out (su/Su, le/Le, él/Él, tu/Tu, te/Te); a clitic joined to the verb, as in "ofrecerle" here, takes none.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR de los ejércitos" (L); "el SEÑOR de los Ejércitos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note: the title keeps the picture of armies (m1). Balanced and Readable capitalize it as a title, as the English "of Armies" does.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân" at every level, the setting span on "CHÚA" only
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note and the Vietnamese Psalms: one title for "the LORD of hosts" and "the LORD of Armies", since "Vạn Quân" ("of the ten thousand armies") already says both.

decisions.choice: "Hê-li", "Hóp-ni", "Phi-nê-a", "Si-lô"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note; "Hê-li" keeps the priest apart from the prophet Elijah, "Ê-li" in the Vietnamese New Testament.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּזְבַּ֖ח אֶלְקָנָ֑ה וְנָתַ֞ן לִפְנִנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּֽלְכָל־בָּנֶ֛יהָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ מָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was the day, and sacrificed Elkanah, and he gave to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters portions.

en.L: And [when] the day came [that] Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and her daughters.
en.B: On the day Elkanah offered his sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
en.R: Each year, on the day Elkanah offered his sacrifice, he gave shares of the meat to his wife Peninnah and to each of her sons and daughters.

es.L: Y [cuando] llegaba el día [en que] Elcana ofrecía sacrificio, daba porciones a Penina su esposa y a todos sus hijos y sus hijas.
es.B: El día en que Elcana ofrecía su sacrificio, daba porciones de la carne a su esposa Penina y a todos los hijos e hijas de ella.
es.R: Cada año, el día en que Elcana ofrecía su sacrificio, les daba su parte de la carne a su esposa Penina y a cada uno de sus hijos e hijas.

fr.L: Et le jour vint où Elqana sacrifiait, et il donnait des parts à Peninna sa femme et à tous ses fils et ses filles.
fr.B: Le jour où Elqana offrait son sacrifice, il donnait des parts de la viande à sa femme Peninna et à tous ses fils et ses filles.
fr.R: Chaque année, le jour où Elqana offrait son sacrifice, il donnait des morceaux de la viande à sa femme Peninna et à chacun de ses fils et de ses filles.

vi.L: Đến ngày Ên-ca-na dâng sinh tế, ông [thường] chia phần cho Phê-ni-na vợ mình và cho tất cả con trai con gái của bà.
vi.B: Vào ngày Ên-ca-na dâng sinh tế, ông thường chia phần thịt cho Phê-ni-na vợ mình và cho tất cả con trai con gái của bà.
vi.R: Mỗi năm, vào ngày Ên-ca-na dâng sinh tế, ông chia phần thịt cho Phê-ni-na vợ mình và cho từng đứa con trai, con gái của bà.

decisions.choice: sacrificed ... portions: the shared meal of a sacrifice
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the sacrifice whose meat the worshipers ate together before Yahweh, after the fat was burned on the altar and the priest had his share (Leviticus 3; 7:11-18, 31-34; Deuteronomy 12:17-18). The head of the family shared out the meat; a portion was one person's share of food at a meal (9:23).

decisions.choice: and it was the day ... he would give: what happened every year
decisions.reason: The opening words and the verb forms that follow describe the custom of each yearly visit (verse 7), not one particular day. The story turns to a single visit in verse 9.

decisions.choice: portions of the meat (Balanced); Each year ... shares of the meat (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the portions were, and Readable adds "Each year" to show that this was a custom (m2).

decisions.choice: imperfect "donnait" (and "offrait", "sacrifiait") for what happened every year
decisions.reason: The verbs describe the custom of each yearly visit, not one day (m2). The French imperfect says this by itself, so French needs no "would" as the English does; Readable keeps the imperfect too, with "Chaque année".

decisions.choice: "thường" for the repeated action
decisions.reason: The Hebrew tells what happened each year (meaning decision); Vietnamese marks the habit with "thường", bracketed at Literal.

source.text: וּלְחַנָּ֕ה יִתֵּ֛ן מָנָ֥ה אַחַ֖ת אַפָּ֑יִם כִּ֤י אֶת־חַנָּה֙ אָהֵ֔ב וַֽיהוָ֖ה סָגַ֥ר רַחְמָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Hannah he gave portion one, of two faces, for Hannah he loved, and Yahweh had closed her womb.

en.L: But to Hannah he would give one double portion, for he loved Hannah, though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had closed her womb.
en.B: But to Hannah he gave a double portion, because he loved her, even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had closed her womb.
en.R: But he gave Hannah twice as much, because he loved her, even though {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not let her have children.

es.L: Pero a Ana le daba una porción doble, porque amaba a Ana, aunque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había cerrado su vientre.
es.B: Pero a Ana le daba una porción doble, porque la amaba, aunque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había cerrado su vientre.
es.R: Pero a Ana le daba el doble, porque la amaba, aunque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no le había permitido tener hijos.

fr.L: Mais à Anne il donnait une part double, car il aimait Anne, bien que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} eût fermé son sein.
fr.B: Mais à Anne il donnait une double part, car il l’aimait, même si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait rendue stérile.
fr.R: Mais à Anne, il donnait deux fois plus, parce qu’il l’aimait, même si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne lui avait pas permis d’avoir des enfants.

vi.L: Nhưng cho An-ne thì ông [thường] cho một phần gấp đôi, vì ông yêu An-ne, dù {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đóng kín tử cung nàng.
vi.B: Nhưng ông cho An-ne một phần gấp đôi, vì ông yêu nàng, dù {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã khiến nàng son sẻ.
vi.R: Nhưng ông cho An-ne gấp đôi, vì ông yêu nàng, dù {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã không cho nàng có con.

decisions.choice: a double portion: a share twice the usual size
alternatives: only one portion, though he loved her
a special portion, a portion of honor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one portion of two faces" (or "of two nostrils"), an expression found only here. It is often read as "a double portion", which fits the reason that follows: he loved her. Others take the word "face" in the sense of sadness or of honor: "only one portion, sadly", since she had no children to share it with, or "a portion of honor". The ancient Greek translation reads "one portion, because she had no child; yet Elkanah loved Hannah more than Peninnah".

decisions.choice: for he loved Hannah, though Yahweh had closed her womb: two facts set side by side
decisions.reason: Both clauses put their subject or object first, which sets them against each other: Elkanah's love was real, but it could not give Hannah a child.

decisions.choice: Yahweh had closed her womb: her barrenness is in God's hands
decisions.reason: The narrator says twice (verses 5 and 6) that Yahweh closed Hannah's womb. Scripture speaks of God closing and opening the womb (Genesis 20:18; 29:31; 30:22), so the one who closed it is the one Hannah must ask (verse 11), and the son, when he comes, is God's gift (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: twice as much; had not let her have children
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a double portion and a closed womb mean.

decisions.choice: "l’avait rendue stérile"
decisions.reason: French "fermer le sein" (Literal) is understood but bookish; Balanced says what it means while keeping the LORD as the one who acts (m3).

decisions.choice: the narrator calls Hannah "nàng"
decisions.reason: As the published Genesis for a young wife (Rachel); it is warm without being informal.

source.text: וְכִֽעֲסַ֤תָּה צָֽרָתָהּ֙ גַּם־כַּ֔עַס בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְּעִמָ֑הּ כִּֽי־סָגַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד רַחְמָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And provoked her her rival, also provocation, in order to make her fret, for had closed Yahweh behind her womb.

en.L: And her rival would provoke her, even sorely, in order to make her fret, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had shut up her womb.
en.B: Her rival kept taunting her bitterly to upset her, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had closed her womb.
en.R: Peninnah, her rival, kept teasing her cruelly to make her miserable, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not let her have children.

es.L: Y su rival la provocaba, y mucho, para hacerla irritarse, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había cerrado su vientre.
es.B: Su rival la mortificaba con dureza para amargarla, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había cerrado su vientre.
es.R: Penina, su rival, se burlaba de ella con crueldad para hacerla sufrir, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no le había permitido tener hijos.

fr.L: Et sa rivale l’irritait, et même fortement, pour la faire frémir, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fermé son sein.
fr.B: Sa rivale ne cessait de la provoquer durement pour la blesser, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait rendue stérile.
fr.R: Peninna, sa rivale, se moquait d’elle méchamment pour la rendre malheureuse, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne lui avait pas permis d’avoir des enfants.

vi.L: Người vợ kình địch của nàng [thường] khiêu khích nàng, thật cay nghiệt, để làm cho nàng bực tức, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đóng kín tử cung nàng.
vi.B: Người vợ kình địch cứ chọc tức nàng cay đắng để làm nàng buồn khổ, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã khiến nàng son sẻ.
vi.R: Phê-ni-na, người vợ kình địch của nàng, cứ trêu chọc nàng cách độc ác cho nàng khổ sở, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã không cho nàng có con.

decisions.choice: rival: a fellow wife
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to press hard or to be hostile. It is used of a second wife in the same home, who was naturally a rival (Leviticus 18:18 uses the related verb of taking a wife's sister "as a rival"). Peninnah is meant (verses 2 and 4).

decisions.choice: provoke: to stir up grief and anger by taunting
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun mean to vex or provoke. Here the noun follows the verb, which makes it strong: she provoked her greatly. The word runs through the story: Peninnah provoked her year after year (verse 7), and Hannah tells Eli that she has been praying out of her anguish and "provocation" (verse 16).

decisions.choice: make her fret: upset her, stir her up inside
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "to thunder" or "to roar". In this form it is used of stirring a person up inside, making her tremble with distress. It has this sense only here.

decisions.choice: Peninnah, her rival ... had not let her have children
decisions.reason: Readable names Peninnah and says plainly what a closed womb means, as in verse 5.

source.text: וְכֵ֨ן יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה מִדֵּ֤י עֲלֹתָהּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֖ן תַּכְעִסֶ֑נָּה וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֹאכַֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And so he did year by year; as often as her going up to [the] house of Yahweh, so she provoked her, and she wept and did not eat.

en.L: And so he did year by year; as often as she went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so she would provoke her, and she would weep and not eat.
en.B: So it went on year after year. Every time Hannah went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Peninnah provoked her, and she wept and would not eat.
en.R: This happened every year. Each time Hannah went up to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Peninnah upset her so much that she cried and would not eat.

es.L: Y así hacía él año tras año; cada vez que ella subía a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, así la provocaba, y ella lloraba y no comía.
es.B: Así sucedía año tras año. Cada vez que Ana subía a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Penina la provocaba, y ella lloraba y no quería comer.
es.R: Esto pasaba todos los años. Cada vez que Ana subía a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Penina la hacía sentir tan mal que ella lloraba y no quería comer.

fr.L: Et il faisait ainsi d’année en année ; chaque fois qu’elle montait à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, ainsi elle l’irritait, et elle pleurait et ne mangeait pas.
fr.B: Cela se répétait chaque année. Chaque fois qu’Anne montait à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, Peninna la provoquait ; alors Anne pleurait et ne voulait plus manger.
fr.R: Cela se passait tous les ans. Chaque fois qu’Anne montait à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, Peninna la blessait tellement qu’elle pleurait et ne voulait pas manger.

vi.L: Năm này qua năm khác ông làm như vậy; mỗi lần nàng đi lên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, người kia lại khiêu khích nàng như thế, và nàng khóc và không ăn.
vi.B: Việc cứ diễn ra như vậy năm này qua năm khác. Mỗi lần An-ne đi lên nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Phê-ni-na lại chọc tức nàng, và nàng khóc, không chịu ăn.
vi.R: Năm nào cũng xảy ra như vậy. Mỗi lần An-ne đi lên nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Phê-ni-na lại làm nàng buồn đến nỗi nàng khóc và không ăn.

decisions.choice: so he did year by year: the same scene was repeated every year
alternatives: so she (Peninnah) did year by year
decisions.reason: The verb is "he did", most naturally Elkanah, who went up and shared out the portions every year (verses 3-5). The ancient Greek reads "she did", meaning Peninnah. Either way the point is that the scene of verses 4-6 happened again on every visit.

decisions.choice: the house of Yahweh: the sanctuary at Shiloh
decisions.reason: The sanctuary at Shiloh is called a house (here; 3:15) and a temple (verse 9). It had doorposts and doors (verse 9; 3:15), so by this time it was more than a tent, though 2:22 still speaks of the tent of meeting. "Went up" is the usual word for travel to a sanctuary.

decisions.choice: she wept and would not eat: what happened each time
decisions.reason: The verbs describe the pattern of each visit. Grief took away Hannah's appetite at the very meal that was meant for rejoicing before Yahweh (Deuteronomy 12:7).

decisions.choice: So it went on (Balanced); This happened (Readable); Hannah, Peninnah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the scene was repeated without naming who "did" it (m1), and they name Hannah and Peninnah where the Hebrew has only "she" and "her".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֜הּ אֶלְקָנָ֣ה אִישָׁ֗הּ חַנָּה֙ לָ֣מֶה תִבְכִּ֗י וְלָ֨מֶה֙ לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְלִ֔י וְלָ֖מֶה יֵרַ֣ע לְבָבֵ֑ךְ הֲל֤וֹא אָֽנֹכִי֙ ט֣וֹב לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Elkanah her husband, Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart bad? Am not I better to you than ten sons?

en.L: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart bad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
en.B: Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why do you not eat? Why are you so downcast? Do I not mean more to you than ten sons?"
en.R: Her husband Elkanah asked her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why will you not eat? Why are you so sad? Am I not worth more to you than ten sons would be?"

es.L: Y Elcana su marido le dijo: «Ana, ¿por qué lloras? ¿Y por qué no comes? ¿Y por qué está mal tu corazón? ¿No soy yo para ti mejor que diez hijos?».
es.B: Su marido Elcana le dijo: «Ana, ¿por qué lloras? ¿Por qué no comes? ¿Por qué estás tan abatida? ¿No valgo yo para ti más que diez hijos?».
es.R: Su marido Elcana le preguntó: «Ana, ¿por qué lloras? ¿Por qué no quieres comer? ¿Por qué estás tan triste? ¿No valgo yo para ti más que diez hijos?».

fr.L: Et Elqana son mari lui dit : « Anne, pourquoi pleures-tu ? Et pourquoi ne manges-tu pas ? Et pourquoi ton cœur est-il mauvais ? Ne suis-je pas meilleur pour toi que dix fils ? »
fr.B: Elqana, son mari, lui dit : « Anne, pourquoi pleures-tu ? Pourquoi ne manges-tu pas ? Pourquoi es-tu si abattue ? Est-ce que je ne compte pas plus pour toi que dix fils ? »
fr.R: Son mari Elqana lui a demandé : « Anne, pourquoi pleures-tu ? Pourquoi est-ce que tu ne veux pas manger ? Pourquoi es-tu si triste ? Est-ce que je ne vaux pas plus pour toi que dix fils ? »

vi.L: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng nói với nàng: "An-ne, sao em khóc? Sao em không ăn? Sao lòng em buồn? Chẳng phải anh tốt cho em hơn mười đứa con trai sao?"
vi.B: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng nói: "An-ne, sao em khóc? Sao em không ăn? Sao em buồn bã như thế? Đối với em, chẳng lẽ anh không quý hơn mười đứa con trai sao?"
vi.R: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng hỏi: "An-ne, sao em khóc? Sao em không chịu ăn? Sao em buồn thế? Đối với em, anh không đáng quý hơn cả mười đứa con trai sao?"

decisions.choice: why is your heart bad: why are you so sad
decisions.reason: When the heart is "bad", a person is downcast or grieved (Nehemiah 2:2, where a sad face shows "badness of heart"). It is not a charge of wickedness.

decisions.choice: Am I not better to you than ten sons?: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: Elkanah means that his love should be enough for her. "Ten" is a round number for a full family; compare Ruth 4:15, where Ruth is "better to you than seven sons". The story does not give Hannah's answer.

decisions.choice: so downcast (Balanced); so sad (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "your heart bad"; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m1).

decisions.choice: Elkanah calls Hannah "em" and himself "anh"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for this couple, and the Genesis note for husband and wife: the Hebrew shows tender concern.

source.text: וַתָּ֣קָם חַנָּ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְלָ֥ה בְשִׁלֹ֖ה וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁתֹ֑ה וְעֵלִ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֗ן יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־הַכִּסֵּ֔א עַל־מְזוּזַ֖ת הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Hannah after her eating in Shiloh and after drinking; and Eli the priest [was] sitting on the seat by [the] doorpost of [the] temple of Yahweh.

en.L: And Hannah rose after her eating in Shiloh and after drinking. And Eli the priest [was] sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Once, when the eating and drinking at Shiloh were over, Hannah got up. Eli the priest sat on his seat beside the doorpost of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.
en.R: One year, after the meal at Shiloh was over, Hannah got up. Eli the priest was sitting on his chair beside the doorway of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

es.L: Y Ana se levantó después de comer en Silo y después de beber. Y el sacerdote Elí [estaba] sentado en la silla junto al poste de la puerta del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Una vez, cuando terminaron de comer y beber en Silo, Ana se levantó. El sacerdote Elí estaba sentado en su silla, junto al marco de la puerta del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Un año, después de la comida en Silo, Ana se levantó. El sacerdote Elí estaba sentado en su silla, junto a la entrada del templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Anne se leva après avoir mangé à Silo et après avoir bu. Et Éli le prêtre [était] assis sur le siège, près du montant de la porte du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Une fois, quand on eut fini de manger et de boire à Silo, Anne se leva. Éli, le prêtre, était assis sur son siège, près du montant de la porte du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Une année, après le repas à Silo, Anne s’est levée. Éli, le prêtre, était assis sur sa chaise, près de l’entrée du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

vi.L: An-ne đứng dậy sau khi đã ăn ở Si-lô và sau khi uống. Thầy tế lễ Hê-li đang ngồi trên ghế bên cạnh trụ cửa đền của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Một lần kia, sau khi ăn uống xong tại Si-lô, An-ne đứng dậy. Bấy giờ thầy tế lễ Hê-li đang ngồi trên ghế của mình, bên cạnh trụ cửa đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Một năm nọ, sau bữa ăn tại Si-lô, An-ne đứng dậy. Lúc ấy thầy tế lễ Hê-li đang ngồi trên ghế bên cửa đền thờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: after the eating and drinking at Shiloh: when the meal was over
alternatives: after she had eaten and drunk
decisions.reason: The words are "after her eating in Shiloh and after drinking". They may mean that Hannah had eaten this time, or simply mark the time: when the sacrificial meal was over. Since verse 7 says she would not eat, and verse 18 says she ate after Eli's blessing, the sense is more likely the end of the family's meal. The ancient Greek reads "after they had eaten".

decisions.choice: the seat: a seat of honor
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for a throne. Eli sits at the entrance of the sanctuary as its chief priest and Israel's leader (4:18), where he can see who comes and goes. He will be sitting on this seat when the news of the ark reaches him, and he will fall from it and die (4:13, 18).

decisions.choice: temple: a great house, a palace
decisions.reason: The word means a palace or a large building and is used of Yahweh's dwelling as the house of a King. Here it names the sanctuary at Shiloh (see verse 7).

decisions.choice: Once (Balanced); One year (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the story now moves from the yearly custom (verses 3-8) to one particular visit.

source.text: וְהִ֖יא מָ֣רַת נָ֑פֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל עַל־יְהוָ֖ה וּבָכֹ֥ה תִבְכֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she [was] bitter of soul, and she prayed to Yahweh, and weeping she wept.

en.L: And she [was] bitter of soul, and she prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and wept and wept.
en.B: She was in deep anguish, and she prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, weeping without restraint.
en.R: Hannah was very sad and upset. She cried and cried as she prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y ella [estaba] amargada de alma, y oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y lloró y lloró.
es.B: Ella estaba profundamente angustiada, y oró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} llorando sin consuelo.
es.R: Ana estaba muy triste y afligida. Lloraba y lloraba mientras oraba {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et elle [avait] l’âme amère, et elle pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et elle pleura, pleura.
fr.B: Elle avait le cœur plein d’amertume ; elle pria {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} en pleurant sans pouvoir s’arrêter.
fr.R: Anne était très triste et bouleversée. Elle pleurait et pleurait pendant qu’elle priait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

vi.L: Nàng [có] tâm hồn cay đắng, và nàng cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và khóc lóc thảm thiết.
vi.B: Lòng nàng đau đớn tột cùng; nàng cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và khóc nức nở.
vi.R: An-ne rất buồn khổ. Nàng vừa cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} vừa khóc mãi.

decisions.choice: bitter of soul: in deep anguish
decisions.reason: Bitterness of the nefesh, the inner self, is deep grief or distress (Job 3:20; 2 Kings 4:27, of the woman of Shunem whose son had died). Naomi asked to be called Mara, "bitter", for the same reason (Ruth 1:20).

decisions.choice: weeping she wept: she wept and wept
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis, a common Hebrew way of strengthening an action: she wept without stopping.

decisions.choice: in deep anguish, weeping without restraint (Balanced); very sad and upset, cried and cried (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "bitter of soul" (m1); Readable keeps the doubled verb as "cried and cried".

decisions.choice: "le cœur plein d’amertume"
decisions.reason: French "amertume" keeps the Hebrew picture of bitterness, which still means deep grief in French, so Balanced can keep it where the English says "in deep anguish".

source.text: וַתִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר וַתֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אִם־רָאֹ֥ה תִרְאֶ֣ה׀בָּעֳנִ֣י אֲמָתֶ֗ךָ וּזְכַרְתַּ֨נִי֙ וְלֹֽא־תִשְׁכַּ֣ח אֶת־אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ זֶ֣רַע אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּנְתַתִּ֤יו לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו וּמוֹרָ֖ה לֹא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she vowed a vow and said, Yahweh of hosts, if indeed you will look on [the] affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant and give to your maidservant seed of men, then I will give him to Yahweh all [the] days of his life, and a razor will not go up on his head.

en.L: And she vowed a vow and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will indeed look on the affliction of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} maidservant and remember me, and not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} maidservant, but give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} maidservant a seed of men, then I will give him to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all the days of his life, and a razor shall not go up on his head."
en.B: She made a vow and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will only look on the misery of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant and remember me, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not forget {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant but will give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant a son, then I will give him to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his whole life, and no razor will ever touch his head."
en.R: She made a solemn promise. She said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant. Please see how I am suffering, and remember me. Do not forget me. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will give me a son, I will give him to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his whole life. No razor will ever cut his hair."

es.L: E hizo un voto y dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, si de veras miras la aflicción de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acuerdas de mí, y no olvidas a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva, sino que das a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva descendencia de varón, yo lo daré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} todos los días de su vida, y navaja no subirá sobre su cabeza».
es.B: Hizo un voto y dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, si {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dignas mirar la aflicción de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acuerdas de mí, si no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} olvidas de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva y le das un hijo varón, yo lo entregaré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} para toda su vida, y jamás pasará navaja por su cabeza».
es.R: Ana hizo una promesa solemne. Dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, yo soy {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sierva. Por favor, mira cuánto sufro y acuérdate de mí. No {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} olvides de mí. Si me das un hijo, yo lo entregaré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} para toda su vida. Nunca le pasarán navaja por la cabeza».

fr.L: Et elle fit un vœu et dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, si vraiment {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} regardes l’humiliation de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante, et si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} te souviens de moi et n’oublies pas {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante, et si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} donnes à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante une semence d’hommes, alors je le donnerai {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} tous les jours de sa vie, et le rasoir ne passera pas sur sa tête. »
fr.B: Elle fit un vœu en disant : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} veux bien regarder la détresse de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante et te souvenir de moi, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’oublies pas {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante et si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lui donnes un fils, je le donnerai {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} pour toute sa vie, et jamais le rasoir ne touchera sa tête. »
fr.R: Elle a fait une promesse solennelle. Elle a dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, je suis {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} servante. S’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît, vois comme je souffre, et souviens-toi de moi. Ne m’oublie pas. Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me donnes un fils, je le donnerai {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} pour toute sa vie. Jamais on ne lui coupera les cheveux. »

vi.L: Nàng khấn nguyện một lời khấn và nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật đoái xem nỗi khốn khổ của tớ gái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhớ đến con và không quên tớ gái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng ban cho tớ gái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một dòng dõi nam nhi, thì con sẽ dâng nó cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trọn mọi ngày của đời nó, và dao cạo sẽ không đưa lên đầu nó."
vi.B: Nàng khấn nguyện rằng: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đoái xem nỗi khổ của đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nhớ đến con, nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không quên đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà ban cho đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một con trai, thì con sẽ dâng nó cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trọn đời, và dao cạo sẽ không bao giờ chạm đến đầu nó."
vi.R: Nàng hứa nguyện cách trọng thể: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, con là đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Xin đoái xem nỗi khổ của con và nhớ đến con. Xin đừng quên con. Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho con một đứa con trai, con sẽ dâng nó cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} suốt đời nó. Sẽ không bao giờ có dao cạo cắt tóc nó."

decisions.choice: she vowed a vow: a solemn promise to God, made with a request
decisions.reason: A vow promised God a gift if he granted what was asked (Genesis 28:20-22; Numbers 21:2; Judges 11:30-31), and it had to be kept (Deuteronomy 23:22-24). A husband could cancel his wife's vow on the day he heard of it (Numbers 30:11-16); Elkanah lets Hannah's vow stand (verse 23).

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: the title of verse 3, now used in prayer
decisions.reason: Hannah calls on God by the title the narrator introduced in verse 3: the King who commands every power in heaven and on earth. She brings the request of one powerless woman to him.

decisions.choice: look on the affliction ... remember me: what God did for Hagar, Leah and Rachel
decisions.reason: Yahweh heard Hagar's affliction (Genesis 16:11) and saw Leah's affliction (Genesis 29:32), and God remembered Rachel and opened her womb (Genesis 30:22). Hannah asks for the same. "Look indeed" doubles the verb: she pleads with God truly to see. The answer comes in verse 19: Yahweh remembered her.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humble way to speak of herself
decisions.reason: 'Amah is a female servant. Hannah calls herself by it three times, as one who depends on her master's kindness (compare Ruth 3:9), and she uses it again to Eli (verse 16).

decisions.choice: seed of men: a male child
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring, and "of men" makes it male: she asks for a son.

decisions.choice: no razor on his head: the sign of a Nazirite
decisions.reason: Uncut hair was the sign that a person was set apart to Yahweh under a Nazirite vow (Numbers 6:5). Numbers 6 describes a vow that a man or woman takes for a set time; Hannah gives her son for life, as Samson was set apart from the womb (Judges 13:5, 7). Hannah does not use the word Nazirite here; see m8.

decisions.choice: I will give him to Yahweh all the days of his life: for life, not for a set time
decisions.reason: Levites served from the age of twenty-five or thirty to fifty (Numbers 4:3; 8:24-25), and a Nazirite vow under Numbers 6 lasted a set time. Samuel is to belong to Yahweh as long as he lives (verses 22 and 28). Hannah turns from speaking to Yahweh to speaking about him ("to Yahweh"), as in a formal promise.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text ends the vow with the razor
alternatives: adds: and he will drink no wine or strong drink (ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds after "his head": "and wine and strong drink he will not drink", the other main Nazirite rule (Numbers 6:3). In verse 22 a Hebrew manuscript of Samuel found at Qumran calls Samuel a Nazirite "for ever, all the days of his life". The Masoretic text has neither, and it is followed here; the razor alone already points to the Nazirite vow. Reviewers should check these readings against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: servant; a son
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "maidservant" and "a seed of men"; Balanced and Readable say "servant" and "a son" (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: Please see ... remember me. Do not forget me. If you will give me a son ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first conditions into plain requests and keeps the "if ... then" form for the heart of the vow: if God gives her a son, she will give him to the LORD. It also says "made a solemn promise" for "vowed a vow" and "No razor will ever cut his hair".

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, without the article, when God is addressed
decisions.reason: French addresses God without the article, so the span holds the name alone, as the published Pentateuch does; the deity pronoun span also goes on the "tu", "te" and "ta" that address God.

decisions.choice: "ta servante" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a woman servant's, used by Hannah of herself in humility (m4). French "servante" carries both the humility and the woman's voice; the masculine "serviteur" of the terms note is for men.

decisions.choice: "tu sierva" at every level
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel: as with "tu siervo" in speech to a king or to God (the Samuel and Psalms notes), the humble self-designation of a woman is "tu sierva" at every level (m4). It is the ordinary courteous word in Spanish and keeps the repeated word of the prayer, where the English says "maidservant" (L) and "servant" (B, R).

decisions.choice: "tớ gái" (L), "đầy tớ" (B, R) for "your maidservant"; Hannah prays as "con" and calls God "Ngài"
decisions.reason: A humble self-description (meaning decision); "tớ gái" keeps the female servant at Literal, "đầy tớ" follows the English "servant". The prayer forms are those of the Vietnamese style guide.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י הִרְבְּתָ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְעֵלִ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֶת־פִּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as she multiplied to pray before Yahweh, and Eli [was] watching her mouth.

en.L: And it was, as she kept on praying before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that Eli was watching her mouth.
en.B: As she went on praying before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Eli was watching her mouth.
en.R: Hannah kept on praying to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for a long time, and Eli was watching her mouth.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras ella seguía orando delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Elí observaba su boca.
es.B: Mientras ella seguía orando delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Elí le observaba la boca.
es.R: Ana estuvo orando {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} mucho tiempo, y Elí le observaba la boca.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme elle prolongeait sa prière devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qu’Éli observait sa bouche.
fr.B: Comme elle prolongeait sa prière devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Éli observait sa bouche.
fr.R: Anne a prié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} longtemps, et Éli regardait sa bouche.

vi.L: Khi nàng cứ cầu nguyện mãi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thì Hê-li quan sát miệng nàng.
vi.B: Trong khi nàng cứ cầu nguyện trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Hê-li để ý miệng nàng.
vi.R: An-ne cầu nguyện với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rất lâu, và Hê-li nhìn miệng nàng.

decisions.choice: she multiplied to pray: she prayed on and on
decisions.reason: The verb means to do much or to keep on: her prayer went on at length.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: at his sanctuary, in his presence
decisions.reason: To pray "before Yahweh" is to pray at the place where he was present with the ark (verses 15 and 19).

decisions.choice: that (Literal); for a long time (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal adds "that" to join the clauses after "And it was"; Readable spells out what "kept on praying" implies.

source.text: וְחַנָּ֗ה הִ֚יא מְדַבֶּ֣רֶת עַל־לִבָּ֔הּ רַ֚ק שְׂפָתֶ֣יהָ נָּע֔וֹת וְקוֹלָ֖הּ לֹ֣א יִשָּׁמֵ֑עַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ עֵלִ֖י לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Hannah, she [was] speaking on her heart; only her lips [were] moving, and her voice was not heard; and thought her Eli to [be] a drunken [woman].

en.L: Now Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips were moving, and her voice was not heard. And Eli took her to be drunk.
en.B: Hannah was speaking within herself. Only her lips moved; no sound of her voice could be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk.
en.R: Hannah was praying silently. Her lips were moving, but no sound came out. So Eli thought she was drunk.

es.L: Pero Ana hablaba en su corazón; solo se movían sus labios, y su voz no se oía. Y Elí la tuvo por ebria.
es.B: Ana hablaba en su interior. Solo movía los labios; no se le oía la voz. Por eso Elí pensó que estaba borracha.
es.R: Ana oraba en silencio. Movía los labios, pero no se oía nada. Por eso Elí pensó que estaba borracha.

fr.L: Or Anne, elle parlait dans son cœur ; seules ses lèvres remuaient, et sa voix ne s’entendait pas. Et Éli la crut ivre.
fr.B: Anne parlait au-dedans d’elle-même : seules ses lèvres remuaient, mais on n’entendait pas sa voix. Éli pensa donc qu’elle était ivre.
fr.R: Anne priait en silence. Ses lèvres bougeaient, mais on n’entendait aucun son. Alors Éli a pensé qu’elle avait trop bu.

vi.L: An-ne nói trong lòng; chỉ có môi nàng mấp máy, còn tiếng nàng thì không nghe thấy. Vì vậy Hê-li tưởng nàng say rượu.
vi.B: An-ne nói thầm trong lòng. Chỉ có đôi môi mấp máy mà không nghe thấy tiếng. Vì thế Hê-li tưởng nàng say rượu.
vi.R: An-ne cầu nguyện thầm. Môi nàng mấp máy nhưng không phát ra tiếng. Vì thế Hê-li tưởng nàng say rượu.

decisions.choice: speaking on her heart: praying silently, within herself
decisions.reason: To speak "on" or "to" one's heart is to speak inwardly (Genesis 24:45, of Abraham's servant praying silently). Prayer was usually spoken aloud (Psalm 3:5), which is why Eli misreads what he sees.

decisions.choice: Eli thought she was drunk
decisions.reason: The feast included wine (verse 9, "after drinking"), and Eli takes her moving lips and silent voice for the mumbling of a woman who has drunk too much.

decisions.choice: speaking within herself (Balanced); praying silently (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ עֵלִ֔י עַד־מָתַ֖י תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִ֑ין הָסִ֥ירִי אֶת־יֵינֵ֖ךְ מֵעָלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Eli, Until when will you make yourself drunk? Put away your wine from upon you.

en.L: And Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you."
en.B: Eli said to her, "How long will you go on being drunk? Get rid of your wine!"
en.R: Eli said to her, "How long are you going to stay drunk? Stop drinking and get sober!"

es.L: Y Elí le dijo: «¿Hasta cuándo estarás ebria? Aparta de ti tu vino».
es.B: Elí le dijo: «¿Hasta cuándo vas a seguir borracha? ¡Deja ya el vino!».
es.R: Elí le dijo: «¿Hasta cuándo vas a seguir borracha? ¡Deja de beber y que se te pase la borrachera!».

fr.L: Et Éli lui dit : « Jusqu’à quand seras-tu ivre ? Ôte ton vin de toi. »
fr.B: Éli lui dit : « Combien de temps vas-tu rester ivre ? Débarrasse-toi de ton vin ! »
fr.R: Éli lui a dit : « Tu vas rester ivre encore longtemps ? Arrête de boire et dessaoule ! »

vi.L: Hê-li nói với nàng: "Bà say cho đến bao giờ? Hãy bỏ rượu của bà khỏi bà đi."
vi.B: Hê-li nói với nàng: "Bà còn say đến bao giờ? Hãy bỏ rượu đi!"
vi.R: Hê-li nói với nàng: "Bà định say đến bao giờ nữa? Hãy thôi uống rượu và tỉnh lại đi!"

decisions.choice: until when: a rebuke
decisions.reason: "Until when?" is a reproach: how long will this go on? (Exodus 10:3; 1 Samuel 16:1).

decisions.choice: put away your wine from you: stop drinking and become sober
decisions.reason: Eli tells her to get rid of the wine that is in her, to sober up, and so also to stop drinking.

decisions.choice: Stop drinking and get sober!
decisions.reason: Readable says what the command means (m2).

decisions.choice: Eli calls Hannah "bà"; she calls him "ông" and herself "tôi"
decisions.reason: A priest at the sanctuary and a married woman he does not know: the Genesis terms note sets "ông", "bà" and "tôi" between people who are not kin. "My lord" is "thưa ông" at Readable and "chúa tôi" at Literal and Balanced (verse 15).

source.text: וַתַּ֨עַן חַנָּ֤ה וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲדֹנִ֔י אִשָּׁ֤ה קְשַׁת־ר֨וּחַ֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וְיַ֥יִן וְשֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Hannah and said, No, my lord, a woman hard of spirit [am] I; and wine and strong drink I have not drunk, and I have poured out my soul before Yahweh.

en.L: And Hannah answered and said, "No, my lord, I [am] a woman hard of spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman deeply troubled in spirit. I have not been drinking wine or beer; I have been pouring out my soul before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: "No, sir," Hannah answered. "I am a very unhappy woman. I have not been drinking wine or beer. I have been telling {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all my sorrow.

es.L: Y Ana respondió y dijo: «No, mi señor; yo [soy] una mujer dura de espíritu. No he bebido vino ni bebida fuerte, sino que he derramado mi alma delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pero Ana respondió: «No, mi señor; soy una mujer profundamente afligida. No he bebido vino ni cerveza; estaba derramando mi alma delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: «No, señor», contestó Ana. «Soy una mujer muy desdichada. No he estado bebiendo vino ni cerveza. Le estaba contando {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} toda mi pena.

fr.L: Et Anne répondit et dit : « Non, mon seigneur, je [suis] une femme à l’esprit accablé. Je n’ai bu ni vin ni boisson forte, mais j’ai répandu mon âme devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Mais Anne répondit : « Non, mon seigneur, je suis une femme profondément troublée. Je n’ai bu ni vin ni bière ; je répandais mon âme devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: « Non, monsieur, a répondu Anne. Je suis une femme très malheureuse. Je n’ai pas bu de vin ni de bière. J’étais en train de dire {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} tout mon chagrin.

vi.L: An-ne đáp và nói: "Không, chúa tôi, tôi [là] một người đàn bà có tâm thần nặng trĩu. Tôi đã không uống rượu hay đồ uống say, nhưng tôi đã dốc đổ linh hồn tôi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Nhưng An-ne đáp: "Thưa chúa tôi, không phải vậy. Tôi là một người đàn bà lòng đầy sầu khổ. Tôi không uống rượu nho hay rượu mạnh; tôi đang dốc đổ lòng mình trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: An-ne đáp: "Thưa ông, không phải vậy. Tôi là một người đàn bà rất đau khổ. Tôi không hề uống rượu. Tôi đang thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mọi nỗi buồn của tôi.

decisions.choice: my lord: a respectful address to a man
decisions.reason: Hannah speaks to the priest as to a man of higher rank; this is not the title used for God.

decisions.choice: hard of spirit: weighed down with trouble
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here. "Hard" is used elsewhere of a heavy lot, such as hard labor (Exodus 6:9). Hannah is not light-headed with drink, as Eli thinks, but heavy with grief.

decisions.choice: strong drink: intoxicating drink other than wine
decisions.reason: Shekhar is any intoxicating drink, such as beer made from grain or drink made from other fruit. Wine and strong drink are named together in the Nazirite law (Numbers 6:3) and in the rule for priests on duty (Leviticus 10:9).

decisions.choice: poured out my soul: told Yahweh all her grief
decisions.reason: To pour out one's soul or heart is to empty out everything one feels before God (Psalm 42:5; 62:9; Lamentations 2:19). Hannah has not been pouring drink; she has been pouring out herself.

decisions.choice: beer
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "strong drink"; Balanced and Readable say "beer", as in Numbers 6:3 (m3).

decisions.choice: sir; a very unhappy woman; telling the LORD all my sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday polite address and gives the sense of the two idioms (m2, m4).

decisions.choice: "mon seigneur" (lowercase) to Eli
decisions.reason: A respectful address to a man (m1), written in two words and lowercase so that it is not read as the title of a bishop or as the Lord; Readable says "monsieur", as the English says "sir".

decisions.choice: "tú" to one person, with "mi señor" (L, B) or "señor" (R) as the courteous address
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as the Samuel terms note and the published Pentateuch: one person is addressed with "tú", the priest and the king included; respect is carried by "mi señor", "mi señor el rey" and "tu siervo" / "tu sierva". Readable says "señor" where the English Readable says "sir".

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi" (L, B), "thưa ông" (R) for "my lord" to a man
decisions.reason: The Genesis terms note sets "chúa tôi" or "ông" for *adoni*; Readable has "sir", which is "thưa ông". Lowercase "chúa" marks a human lord.

decisions.choice: "rượu nho hay rượu mạnh" (B); "rượu" (R) for wine and strong drink
decisions.reason: The English "beer" names a drink Vietnamese readers would not picture at an ancient sanctuary; "rượu mạnh" says intoxicating drink (meaning decision), and Readable folds the pair into "rượu".

source.text: אַל־תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לִפְנֵ֖י בַּת־בְּלִיָּ֑עַל כִּֽי־מֵרֹ֥ב שִׂיחִ֛י וְכַעְסִ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not give your maidservant before [the] face of a daughter of worthlessness, for from [the] abundance of my complaint and my provocation I have spoken until now.

en.L: Do not regard your maidservant as a daughter of worthlessness, for out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation I have spoken until now."
en.B: Do not take your servant for a worthless woman. All this time I have been speaking out of my great anguish and distress."
en.R: Please do not think I am a wicked woman. I have been praying here so long because I am so troubled and hurt."

es.L: No tengas a tu sierva por una hija de perversidad, porque por la abundancia de mi queja y de mi aflicción he hablado hasta ahora».
es.B: No tomes a tu sierva por una mujer perversa. Todo este tiempo he estado hablando por mi gran angustia y aflicción».
es.R: Por favor, no pienses que soy una mala mujer. He estado orando aquí tanto tiempo porque estoy muy angustiada y dolida».

fr.L: Ne mets pas ta servante au rang d’une fille de vaurien, car c’est de l’abondance de ma plainte et de mon chagrin que j’ai parlé jusqu’à maintenant. »
fr.B: Ne prends pas ta servante pour une femme de rien. Si j’ai parlé si longtemps, c’est à cause de ma grande angoisse et de ma détresse. »
fr.R: Je t’en prie, ne pense pas que je suis une mauvaise femme. Si je prie ici depuis si longtemps, c’est parce que j’ai beaucoup de peine et que je suis blessée. »

vi.L: Xin đừng xem tớ gái của ông như một đứa con gái của sự gian tà, vì tôi đã nói cho đến bây giờ là do quá nhiều nỗi than thở và nỗi tức tối của tôi."
vi.B: Xin đừng coi đầy tớ của ông là người đàn bà hư hỏng. Bấy lâu nay tôi nói là vì lòng tôi quá đau đớn và sầu khổ."
vi.R: Xin ông đừng nghĩ tôi là người đàn bà xấu xa. Tôi cầu nguyện ở đây lâu như vậy là vì tôi quá buồn khổ và đau lòng."

decisions.choice: do not give your maidservant before a daughter of worthlessness: do not take me for a worthless woman
decisions.reason: "Daughter of" describes character: a "daughter of belial" is a woman of no worth, a disgrace. The same word is used of Eli's own sons, "sons of belial" (2:12).

decisions.choice: my complaint: troubled thoughts poured out in words
decisions.reason: Siach is anxious thinking and the outpouring of it in words, often in prayer (Psalm 142:3; Job 7:13).

decisions.choice: my provocation: the grief of being provoked
decisions.reason: It is the same word as in verses 6 and 7: what Peninnah's taunts have done to her.

decisions.choice: anguish and distress (Balanced); so troubled and hurt (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "complaint" and "provocation"; Balanced and Readable give their sense (m2, m3). Readable adds "here so long" for "until now".

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַן עֵלִ֛י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְכִ֣י לְשָׁל֑וֹם וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל יִתֵּן֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣לָתֵ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתְּ מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Eli and said, Go in peace, and [the] God of Israel grant your petition which you have asked from with him.

en.L: And Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Eli answered, "Go in peace. May the God of Israel grant what you have asked of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Then Eli said, "Go in peace. May the God of Israel give you what you have asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for."

es.L: Y Elí respondió y dijo: «Ve en paz, y que el Dios de Israel te conceda la petición que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has pedido».
es.B: Elí le respondió: «Ve en paz. Que el Dios de Israel te conceda lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has pedido».
es.R: Entonces Elí le dijo: «Ve en paz. Que el Dios de Israel te dé lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} has pedido».

fr.L: Et Éli répondit et dit : « Va en paix, et que le Dieu d’Israël t’accorde la demande que tu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as demandée. »
fr.B: Éli lui répondit : « Va en paix. Que le Dieu d’Israël t’accorde ce que tu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as demandé. »
fr.R: Alors Éli lui a dit : « Va en paix. Que le Dieu d’Israël te donne ce que tu {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} as demandé. »

vi.L: Hê-li đáp và nói: "Hãy đi bình an, và nguyện Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên ban cho bà điều bà đã cầu xin nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.B: Hê-li đáp: "Hãy đi bình an. Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên ban cho bà điều bà đã cầu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."
vi.R: Hê-li nói: "Hãy về bình an. Nguyện Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên ban cho bà điều bà đã xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."

decisions.choice: may he grant: a blessing
alternatives: the God of Israel will grant
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish, "may he grant", or as a promise, "he will grant". Spoken by the priest as he sends her away, it is a blessing, and Hannah receives it with hope (verse 18).

decisions.choice: your petition that you asked: the key word of the story
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from sha'al, "to ask". The word returns when Hannah names her son (verse 20) and when she gives him to Yahweh (verses 27-28), and it sounds like the name Saul, sha'ul, "asked for", the king whom Israel will ask for (8:10; 12:13).

decisions.choice: Go in peace: a farewell blessing
decisions.reason: Shalom is wholeness and well-being. The words send her away with good wishes (Judges 18:6; 2 Kings 5:19).

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר תִּמְצָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ הָאִשָּׁ֤ה לְדַרְכָּהּ֙ וַתֹּאכַ֔ל וּפָנֶ֥יהָ לֹא־הָיוּ־לָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, May find your maidservant favor in your eyes. And went the woman on her way, and she ate, and her face was not to her anymore.

en.L: And she said, "May your maidservant find favor in your eyes." And the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer [sad].
en.B: She said, "May your servant find favor in your sight." Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer downcast.
en.R: Hannah answered, "Thank you, sir. I hope you will always think well of me." Then she went away and ate something, and she no longer looked sad.

es.L: Y ella dijo: «Halle tu sierva gracia ante tus ojos». Y la mujer se fue por su camino y comió, y su rostro ya no estuvo [triste].
es.B: Ella dijo: «Que tu sierva halle favor ante tus ojos». Luego la mujer se fue por su camino y comió, y su rostro ya no estaba abatido.
es.R: Ana respondió: «Gracias, señor. Ojalá siempre pienses bien de mí». Luego se fue, comió algo y ya no parecía triste.

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Que ta servante trouve grâce à tes yeux. » Et la femme s’en alla son chemin, et elle mangea, et son visage ne fut plus [triste].
fr.B: Elle dit : « Que ta servante trouve grâce à tes yeux. » Puis la femme s’en alla, elle mangea, et son visage n’était plus abattu.
fr.R: Anne a répondu : « Merci, monsieur. J’espère que tu penseras toujours du bien de moi. » Puis elle est partie et elle a mangé quelque chose. Elle n’avait plus l’air triste.

vi.L: Nàng nói: "Nguyện tớ gái của ông được ơn trong mắt ông." Rồi người đàn bà đi đường mình và ăn, và mặt nàng không còn [buồn] nữa.
vi.B: Nàng nói: "Nguyện đầy tớ của ông được ơn trước mặt ông." Rồi người đàn bà ra đi, ăn uống, và nét mặt nàng không còn ủ rũ nữa.
vi.R: An-ne đáp: "Cảm ơn ông. Mong ông luôn nghĩ tốt về tôi." Rồi nàng đi ăn, và nét mặt nàng không còn buồn nữa.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humbler word
decisions.reason: Here she uses shifchah, a humbler word for a servant girl than the 'amah of verses 11 and 16 (compare Ruth 2:13). She answers the priest with thanks and respect.

decisions.choice: find favor in your eyes: may you think kindly of me
decisions.reason: This is a polite way to thank someone or to ask that they stay kind (Genesis 33:15; Ruth 2:13).

decisions.choice: her face was no longer hers: she no longer looked sad
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "her face was not to her anymore", a short expression whose sense is clear from the story: the downcast face of verses 7-8 was gone. The ancient Greek reads "her face did not fall anymore". Hannah ate the meal she had refused (verse 7), because her grief had lifted.

decisions.choice: her face was no longer [sad]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the word the short Hebrew expression implies (m3).

decisions.choice: Thank you, sir. I hope you will always think well of me.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the polite formula (m2) and puts Hannah's words in the first person.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֛בוּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־בֵּיתָ֖ם הָרָמָ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤דַע אֶלְקָנָה֙ אֶת־חַנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽזְכְּרֶ֖הָ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early in the morning and bowed down before Yahweh, and they returned and came to their house, to Ramah. And knew Elkanah Hannah his wife, and remembered her Yahweh.

en.L: And they rose early in the morning and worshiped before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remembered her.
en.B: Early the next morning they worshiped before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and then went back home to Ramah. Elkanah lay with his wife Hannah, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remembered her.
en.R: Early the next morning the family worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then they went back home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with his wife Hannah, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remembered her and answered her prayer.

es.L: Y se levantaron de madrugada y adoraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y volvieron y llegaron a su casa en Ramá. Y Elcana conoció a Ana su esposa, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se acordó de ella.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, muy temprano, adoraron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y luego regresaron a su casa en Ramá. Elcana se unió a su esposa Ana, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se acordó de ella.
es.R: Muy temprano a la mañana siguiente, la familia adoró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Después regresaron a su casa en Ramá. Elcana tuvo relaciones con su esposa Ana, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se acordó de ella y respondió a su oración.

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent de bon matin et se prosternèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ils s’en retournèrent et vinrent à leur maison, à Rama. Et Elqana connut Anne sa femme, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se souvint d’elle.
fr.B: Le lendemain, de bon matin, ils adorèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, puis ils rentrèrent chez eux à Rama. Elqana s’unit à sa femme Anne, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se souvint d’elle.
fr.R: Le lendemain, très tôt, toute la famille a adoré {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Puis ils sont rentrés chez eux, à Rama. Elqana a dormi avec sa femme Anne, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} s’est souvenu d’elle et a répondu à sa prière.

vi.L: Họ dậy sớm vào buổi sáng và thờ lạy trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, rồi trở về và đến nhà mình tại Ra-ma. Ên-ca-na ăn ở với An-ne vợ mình, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nhớ đến nàng.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau họ dậy sớm, thờ phượng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, rồi trở về nhà tại Ra-ma. Ên-ca-na ăn ở với An-ne vợ mình, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nhớ đến nàng.
vi.R: Sáng sớm hôm sau cả nhà thờ phượng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Rồi họ trở về nhà ở Ra-ma. Ên-ca-na ăn ở với An-ne vợ mình, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nhớ đến nàng và nhậm lời nàng cầu xin.

decisions.choice: Ramah: the town of verse 1
decisions.reason: Ramah, "the height", is the short name of Ramathaim-zophim (verse 1). It stays Samuel's home all his life (7:17; 25:1).

decisions.choice: knew: had sexual relations with
decisions.reason: To "know" one's wife is a gentle way of speaking of married love (Genesis 4:1).

decisions.choice: Yahweh remembered her: he acted on her behalf
decisions.reason: When God "remembers" someone, he does not recall what he had forgotten; he turns to act for them, as he remembered Noah (Genesis 8:1) and Rachel (Genesis 30:22). Hannah had asked him to remember her (verse 11).

decisions.choice: lay with (Balanced); slept with ... and answered her prayer (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for "knew" (m2). Readable adds what Yahweh's remembering meant for Hannah (m3).

decisions.choice: "ăn ở với" for "knew" at every level
decisions.reason: The idiom means sexual relations (meaning decision); "biết" would not say that in Vietnamese, while "ăn ở với" is the plain, modest word for husband and wife.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ לִתְקֻפ֣וֹת הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתַּ֥הַר חַנָּ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־שְׁמוֹ֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה שְׁאִלְתִּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] turnings of the days, and conceived Hannah and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, for from Yahweh I asked him.

en.L: And it was at the turning of the days [that] Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, for [she said], "From {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} I asked him."
en.B: In due time Hannah became pregnant and bore a son. She called him Samuel, for she said,"I asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for him."
en.R: Hannah became pregnant, and when the time came she had a son. She named him Samuel. She said, "I asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for him."

es.L: Y sucedió, al cumplirse los días, [que] Ana concibió y dio a luz un hijo, y llamó su nombre Samuel, porque [dijo]: «{{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} se lo pedí».
es.B: A su debido tiempo Ana quedó embarazada y dio a luz un hijo. Lo llamó Samuel, porque dijo: «Se lo pedí {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».
es.R: Ana quedó embarazada, y cuando llegó el momento tuvo un hijo. Le puso por nombre Samuel. Dijo: «Se lo pedí {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et il arriva, au retour des jours, qu’Anne conçut et enfanta un fils, et elle appela son nom Samuel, car [elle dit] : « C’est {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} que je l’ai demandé. »
fr.B: Au temps voulu, Anne devint enceinte et mit au monde un fils. Elle l’appela Samuel, car elle disait : « Je l’ai demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Anne est tombée enceinte et, le moment venu, elle a eu un fils. Elle l’a appelé Samuel. Elle disait : « Je l’ai demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. »

vi.L: Đến kỳ của những ngày [ấy], An-ne thụ thai và sinh một con trai, và nàng đặt tên nó là Sa-mu-ên, vì [nàng nói]: "Tôi đã cầu xin nó từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.B: Đến kỳ, An-ne có thai và sinh một con trai. Nàng đặt tên con là Sa-mu-ên, vì nàng nói: "Tôi đã cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} để có nó."
vi.R: An-ne có thai, và đến ngày nàng sinh một con trai. Nàng đặt tên con là Sa-mu-ên. Nàng nói: "Tôi đã xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho tôi đứa con này."

decisions.choice: at the turning of the days: when the time came round
alternatives: at the turn of the year
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the turn of the year (Exodus 34:22; 2 Chronicles 24:23). It may mean that by the next yearly visit Hannah had her son, or simply that she gave birth when the time of her pregnancy was complete. Either way the child came in God's time.

decisions.choice: Samuel: a name explained by "asked"
decisions.reason: The name Samuel, Shemu'el, most likely means "name of God" (some hear in it "heard by God"). Hannah's explanation, "from Yahweh I asked him", is a play on sound rather than a definition: the verb sha'al, "ask", echoes in the name. Scripture often gives a name its meaning from the story of a birth (Genesis 29:32-35). The same verb sounds even more like Saul, sha'ul, "asked for" (see verse 17).

decisions.choice: for from Yahweh I asked him: Hannah's own words
decisions.reason: The sentence switches to "I", so these are the words Hannah said as she named him.

decisions.choice: for [she said] (Literal); for she said (Balanced); She said (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves straight into Hannah's words without "she said"; every level supplies it so the reader knows who speaks (m3).

decisions.choice: "Sa-mu-ên", with no explanation of the sound added
decisions.reason: As the English, every level gives Hannah's words alone; the meaning decision explains the play on "asked", which the Vietnamese words cannot echo.

source.text: וַיַּ֛עַל הָאִ֥ישׁ אֶלְקָנָ֖ה וְכָל־בֵּית֑וֹ לִזְבֹּ֧חַ לַֽיהוָ֛ה אֶת־זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֶת־נִדְרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the man Elkanah and all his house to sacrifice to Yahweh the sacrifice of the days and his vow.
