en.L: And the man Elkanah and all his house went up to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the yearly sacrifice and his vow.
en.B: Elkanah went up with his whole household to offer {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the yearly sacrifice and to pay his vow.
en.R: Once again Elkanah went up with all his family to offer the yearly sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to keep his vow.

es.L: Y subió el hombre Elcana y toda su casa para sacrificar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} el sacrificio anual y su voto.
es.B: Elcana subió con toda su familia para ofrecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} el sacrificio anual y cumplir su voto.
es.R: Una vez más Elcana subió con toda su familia para ofrecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} el sacrificio de cada año y para cumplir su voto.

fr.L: Et l’homme Elqana monta avec toute sa maison pour sacrifier {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} le sacrifice annuel et son vœu.
fr.B: Elqana monta avec toute sa famille pour offrir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} le sacrifice annuel et accomplir son vœu.
fr.R: Comme chaque année, Elqana est monté à Silo avec toute sa famille pour offrir le sacrifice annuel {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et pour tenir sa promesse.

vi.L: Người chồng là Ên-ca-na cùng cả nhà mình đi lên để dâng cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sinh tế hằng năm và [lễ vật] khấn nguyện của mình.
vi.B: Ên-ca-na cùng cả nhà đi lên dâng cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sinh tế hằng năm và làm trọn lời khấn nguyện của mình.
vi.R: Ên-ca-na lại cùng cả gia đình đi lên dâng sinh tế hằng năm cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và giữ lời khấn nguyện của mình.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of the days: the yearly sacrifice
decisions.reason: "Days" means a year, as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: his vow: a vow of Elkanah's own, or his share in Hannah's vow
decisions.reason: The story has not mentioned a vow of Elkanah's. He may have made one of his own, perhaps in thanks for the son. Or "his vow" may be Hannah's vow, which he had let stand as her husband and so made his own (Numbers 30:11-16). A vow was often paid with a sacrifice (Leviticus 7:16; Deuteronomy 12:6).

decisions.choice: to pay his vow (Balanced); to keep his vow (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "his vow" to the verb "sacrifice"; Balanced and Readable supply a verb that fits a vow. Readable adds "Once again" to show that this is the next yearly visit.

source.text: וְחַנָּ֖ה לֹ֣א עָלָ֑תָה כִּֽי־אָמְרָ֣ה לְאִישָׁ֗הּ עַ֣ד יִגָּמֵ֤ל הַנַּ֨עַר֙ וַהֲבִאֹתִ֗יו וְנִרְאָה֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיָ֥שַׁב שָׁ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, Until is weaned the boy; and I will bring him, and he will appear [before the] face of Yahweh and dwell there until forever.

en.L: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "[Not] until the boy is weaned; then I will bring him, and he will appear before the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and dwell there forever."
en.B: But Hannah did not go. She told her husband, "Once the boy is weaned, I will bring him to appear before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he will stay there for the rest of his life."
en.R: But Hannah stayed home. She told her husband, "When the boy no longer needs to nurse, I will take him to Shiloh. He will be presented to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and live there for the rest of his life."

es.L: Pero Ana no subió, porque dijo a su marido: «[No] hasta que el niño sea destetado; entonces lo llevaré, y se presentará ante el rostro {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se quedará allí para siempre».
es.B: Pero Ana no fue. Le dijo a su marido: «Cuando el niño esté destetado, lo llevaré para que se presente delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y se quedará allí el resto de su vida».
es.R: Pero Ana se quedó en casa. Le dijo a su marido: «Cuando el niño ya no necesite mamar, lo llevaré a Silo. Será presentado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y vivirá allí el resto de su vida».

fr.L: Mais Anne ne monta pas, car elle dit à son mari : « [Pas] avant que l’enfant soit sevré ; alors je l’amènerai, et il paraîtra devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et il demeurera là pour toujours. »
fr.B: Mais Anne n’y alla pas. Elle dit à son mari : « Quand l’enfant sera sevré, je l’amènerai pour qu’il paraisse devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et il restera là-bas pour le reste de sa vie. »
fr.R: Mais Anne est restée à la maison. Elle a dit à son mari : « Quand l’enfant n’aura plus besoin d’être allaité, je l’emmènerai à Silo. Il sera présenté {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et il vivra là-bas toute sa vie. »

vi.L: Nhưng An-ne không đi lên, vì nàng nói với chồng: "[Đợi] cho đến khi đứa trẻ thôi bú; rồi tôi sẽ đem nó lên, và nó sẽ ra mắt trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và ở đó mãi mãi."
vi.B: Nhưng An-ne không đi. Nàng nói với chồng: "Khi nào đứa trẻ thôi bú, em sẽ đem nó lên để ra mắt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và nó sẽ ở lại đó suốt đời."
vi.R: Nhưng An-ne ở nhà. Nàng nói với chồng: "Khi nào con thôi bú, em sẽ đưa con lên Si-lô. Con sẽ được dâng cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và sống ở đó suốt đời."

decisions.choice: weaned: perhaps two or three years old
decisions.reason: Children were nursed much longer than is usual today, often for two or three years, and a feast could mark the weaning (Genesis 21:8). Samuel would still be a small child when he came to Shiloh (verse 24), but old enough to be cared for by others and to serve (2:11, 18).

decisions.choice: appear before Yahweh: be presented at his sanctuary
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Israel's men appearing before Yahweh at the yearly feasts (Exodus 23:17; 34:23; Deuteronomy 16:16). Samuel will appear there not for a feast but to stay.

decisions.choice: until forever: for good, all his life
decisions.reason: "Until forever" here means permanently, for the whole of his life, as Hannah vowed (verse 11) and says again in verse 28.

decisions.choice: [Not] until
decisions.reason: Hannah's words begin with "until", leaving "I will not go up" to be understood from the start of the verse; Literal supplies "Not".

decisions.choice: stayed home; no longer needs to nurse; to Shiloh
decisions.reason: Readable explains "weaned" and names the place where the LORD's house was (verse 3).

decisions.choice: Hannah calls herself "em" to Elkanah (B, R); Literal keeps "tôi"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: Hannah calls her husband "anh" and herself "em"; Literal keeps the plain first person, as the Genesis note allows for a wife's formal speech.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהּ֩ אֶלְקָנָ֨ה אִישָׁ֜הּ עֲשִׂ֧י הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינַ֗יִךְ שְׁבִי֙ עַד־גָּמְלֵ֣ךְ אֹת֔וֹ אַ֛ךְ יָקֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־דְּבָר֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וַתֵּ֣ינֶק אֶת־בְּנָ֔הּ עַד־גָּמְלָ֖הּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Elkanah her husband, Do the good in your eyes; stay until you have weaned him; only may establish Yahweh his word. And stayed the woman and nursed her son until she weaned him.

en.L: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what [is] good in your eyes; stay until you have weaned him; only may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} establish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word." So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.
en.B: Her husband Elkanah told her, "Do what seems best to you. Stay at home until you have weaned him. Only may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word come true." So the woman stayed home and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
en.R: Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Do whatever you think is best. Stay here until he no longer needs to nurse. I only pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said." So Hannah stayed home and nursed her son until he was old enough to stop.

es.L: Y Elcana su marido le dijo: «Haz lo que [es] bueno a tus ojos; quédate hasta que lo hayas destetado; solamente que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} confirme {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra». Y la mujer se quedó y amamantó a su hijo hasta que lo destetó.
es.B: Su marido Elcana le dijo: «Haz lo que te parezca mejor. Quédate en casa hasta que lo hayas destetado. Solo pido que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga realidad {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra». Así que la mujer se quedó en casa y amamantó a su hijo hasta destetarlo.
es.R: Su marido Elcana le dijo: «Haz lo que te parezca mejor. Quédate aquí hasta que el niño ya no necesite mamar. Solo pido que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga lo que ha dicho». Así que Ana se quedó en casa y amamantó a su hijo hasta que tuvo edad para dejar el pecho.

fr.L: Et Elqana son mari lui dit : « Fais ce qui [est] bon à tes yeux ; reste jusqu’à ce que tu l’aies sevré ; seulement, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accomplisse {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole. » Et la femme resta et allaita son fils jusqu’à ce qu’elle l’eût sevré.
fr.B: Son mari Elqana lui répondit : « Fais ce qui te semble bon. Reste à la maison jusqu’à ce que tu l’aies sevré. Seulement, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} réalise {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole ! » La femme resta donc et allaita son fils jusqu’à ce qu’elle l’eût sevré.
fr.R: Son mari Elqana lui a dit : « Fais ce qui te semble le mieux. Reste ici jusqu’à ce qu’il n’ait plus besoin d’être allaité. Je prie seulement pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fasse ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit. » Alors Anne est restée à la maison et elle a allaité son fils jusqu’à ce qu’il soit assez grand pour arrêter.

vi.L: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng nói với nàng: "Hãy làm điều tốt trong mắt em; hãy ở lại cho đến khi em cho nó thôi bú; chỉ nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm vững lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}." Vậy người đàn bà ở lại và cho con bú cho đến khi nàng cho nó thôi bú.
vi.B: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng bảo: "Em thấy thế nào là tốt thì cứ làm. Hãy ở nhà cho đến khi con thôi bú. Chỉ nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm cho lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được thành tựu." Vậy người đàn bà ở nhà nuôi con cho đến khi con thôi bú.
vi.R: Ên-ca-na chồng nàng nói: "Em thấy sao là tốt nhất thì cứ làm. Hãy ở nhà cho đến khi con thôi bú. Anh chỉ cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} làm điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán." Vậy An-ne ở nhà cho con bú cho đến khi con đủ lớn để thôi bú.

decisions.choice: Do what is good in your eyes: Elkanah agrees to her plan
decisions.reason: As her husband he could have cancelled her vow (Numbers 30:11-16). Instead he lets her decide when to bring the boy, and so he confirms the vow.

decisions.choice: may Yahweh establish his word: the Hebrew text
alternatives: may Yahweh establish what has gone out of your mouth (ancient Greek, Qumran)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "his word", meaning Yahweh's. No word of Yahweh about the boy has been reported; it may mean Eli's blessing taken as Yahweh's promise (verse 17), or Yahweh's purpose in giving the child. The ancient Greek translation and a Hebrew manuscript from Qumran read "what has gone out of your mouth", that is, may Yahweh help Hannah to keep her vow. The Hebrew text is followed here; reviewers should check the readings.

decisions.choice: make his word come true (Balanced); do what he has said (Readable); Hannah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for the LORD to "establish" a word. Readable names Hannah for "the woman" and explains "weaned".

source.text: וַתַּעֲלֵ֨הוּ עִמָּ֜הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר גְּמָלַ֗תּוּ בְּפָרִ֤ים שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ וְאֵיפָ֨ה אַחַ֥ת קֶ֨מַח֙ וְנֵ֣בֶל יַ֔יִן וַתְּבִאֵ֥הוּ בֵית־יְהוָ֖ה שִׁל֑וֹ וְהַנַּ֖עַר נָֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls and one ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him [to the] house of Yahweh [at] Shiloh; and the boy [was] a boy.

en.L: And she brought him up with her when she had weaned him, with three bulls, and one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [at] Shiloh; and the boy [was] young.
en.B: Once she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with three bulls, {{units:about 20 quarts|an ephah}} of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Shiloh. The boy was still young.
en.R: When Samuel was weaned, Hannah took him with her to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Shiloh. She also took three bulls, {{units:about 20 quarts|an ephah}} of flour, and a leather bag of wine. Samuel was still very young.

es.L: Y lo subió consigo cuando lo hubo destetado, con tres toros, un efa de harina y un odre de vino, y lo llevó a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [en] Silo; y el niño [era] pequeño.
es.B: Cuando lo hubo destetado, lo subió consigo junto con tres toros, {{units:unos 22 litros|un efa}} de harina y un odre de vino, y lo llevó a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Silo. El niño todavía era pequeño.
es.R: Cuando Samuel fue destetado, Ana lo llevó consigo a la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Silo. También llevó tres toros, {{units:unos 22 litros|un efa}} de harina y una bolsa de cuero llena de vino. Samuel era todavía muy pequeño.

fr.L: Et elle le fit monter avec elle quand elle l’eut sevré, avec trois taureaux, et un épha de farine, et une outre de vin, et elle l’amena à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [à] Silo ; et l’enfant [était] jeune.
fr.B: Une fois qu’elle l’eut sevré, elle l’emmena avec elle, ainsi que trois taureaux, {{units:environ 22 litres|un épha}} de farine et une outre de vin, et elle l’amena à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} à Silo. L’enfant était encore jeune.
fr.R: Quand Samuel a été sevré, Anne l’a emmené avec elle à la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, à Silo. Elle a aussi emporté trois taureaux, {{units:environ 22 litres|un épha}} de farine et un sac de cuir rempli de vin. Samuel était encore très petit.

vi.L: Khi đã cho nó thôi bú, nàng đem nó lên với mình, cùng với ba con bò đực, một ê-pha bột và một bầu da rượu, và đem nó vào nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [tại] Si-lô; và đứa trẻ [còn] nhỏ.
vi.B: Khi con đã thôi bú, nàng đem con lên cùng với ba con bò đực, {{units:khoảng 22 lít|một ê-pha}} bột và một bầu da rượu, đưa con vào nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tại Si-lô. Đứa trẻ vẫn còn nhỏ.
vi.R: Khi Sa-mu-ên thôi bú, An-ne đem con lên nhà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở Si-lô. Nàng cũng đem theo ba con bò đực, {{units:khoảng 22 lít|một ê-pha}} bột và một túi da đựng rượu. Sa-mu-ên vẫn còn rất nhỏ.

decisions.choice: three bulls: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "three bulls", but verse 25 speaks of "the bull". The ancient Greek translation and a Hebrew manuscript from Qumran read "a bull three years old", which differs only slightly in the Hebrew letters and fits verse 25. With three bulls, "the bull" of verse 25 is the one offered when the boy was presented. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: an ephah of flour and a skin of wine: a generous offering
decisions.reason: An ephah was about 20 quarts. Flour and wine went with a bull offered as a sacrifice (Numbers 15:8-10 asks three tenths of an ephah of flour and half a hin of wine for each bull); Hannah brings far more. The word for the wine container can mean a leather skin or a large clay jar (Jeremiah 13:12).

decisions.choice: the boy was a boy: the child was still young
decisions.reason: Repeating the word stresses how young he was: a little child, just weaned, given to the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: Samuel; a leather bag of wine
decisions.reason: Readable names Samuel and Hannah for "him" and "she", and says what a skin was.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 22 litres|un épha}}
decisions.reason: French readers use metric measures, so the default gives the ephah in litres (22 litres, the value of the Pentateuch note), with the original measure as the alternative; Literal keeps "un épha", as the English Literal keeps "ephah". This holds for every measure in 1 Samuel.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 22 litros|un efa}}; Literal "un efa"
decisions.reason: For 1 and 2 Samuel, as the Pentateuch note: where the English converts a measure, Spanish converts to metric (ephah 22 litres, shekel 11,5 g, cubit 45 cm), with the original unit as the reader setting; Literal keeps the original unit, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 22 lít" by default, "một ê-pha" with the Measures setting; Literal keeps "một ê-pha"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses metric measures by default, at the value the Samuel terms note sets for an ephah.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת־הַפָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־הַנַּ֖עַר אֶל־עֵלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to Eli.

en.L: And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to Eli.
en.B: They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
en.R: After they had killed the bull as a sacrifice, they brought the boy to Eli.

es.L: Y degollaron el toro, y trajeron al niño a Elí.
es.B: Sacrificaron el toro y llevaron al niño ante Elí.
es.R: Después de matar el toro como sacrificio, llevaron al niño a Elí.

fr.L: Et ils égorgèrent le taureau, et ils amenèrent l’enfant à Éli.
fr.B: Ils égorgèrent le taureau et amenèrent l’enfant à Éli.
fr.R: Ils ont tué le taureau pour l’offrir en sacrifice, puis ils ont amené l’enfant à Éli.

vi.L: Họ giết con bò đực, và đem đứa trẻ đến với Hê-li.
vi.B: Họ giết con bò đực rồi đem đứa trẻ đến với Hê-li.
vi.R: Sau khi giết con bò đực làm sinh tế, họ đưa đứa trẻ đến với Hê-li.

decisions.choice: slaughtered the bull: the sacrifice that marked the boy's presentation
decisions.reason: The bull was killed as an offering, probably a burnt offering given wholly to Yahweh (Leviticus 1:3-5), as Samuel himself was being given wholly to him. On the number of bulls, see verse 24.

decisions.choice: as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Readable says why the bull was killed.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י חֵ֥י נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֲנִ֣י הָאִשָּׁ֗ה הַנִּצֶּ֤בֶת עִמְּכָה֙ בָּזֶ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Please, my lord, [by the] life of your soul, my lord, I [am] the woman standing with you in this [place] to pray to Yahweh.

en.L: And she said, "Please, my lord! [As] your soul lives, my lord, I [am] the woman who stood beside you here, praying to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Hannah said, "Pardon me, my lord! As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who once stood beside you here, praying to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Hannah said to Eli, "Excuse me, sir. I promise you, I am the woman who stood here next to you and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: please, my lord: asking leave to speak
decisions.reason: Bi, "please" or "pardon me", is how one asks a superior to listen (Genesis 43:20; Judges 6:13).

decisions.choice: as your soul lives: an oath, "as surely as you live"
decisions.reason: Swearing by a person's life was a solemn way to assure them that what follows is true (17:55; 20:3; 25:26). Some years have passed, and Hannah assures Eli that she is the woman he saw.

decisions.choice: the woman who stood beside you here: the scene of verses 9-18
decisions.reason: Hannah points back to the place and the prayer that Eli saw, so that he will see what Yahweh has done.

decisions.choice: Excuse me, sir. I promise you
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday polite address and gives the sense of the oath (m2). It names Eli as the one she speaks to.

decisions.choice: granted him ... granted: handed over in answer to asking
decisions.reason: The verb is sha'al again, "ask", in a form that means to let someone have what was asked, to grant or hand over (Exodus 12:36 uses it of the Egyptians giving Israel what it asked). It is not a loan to be taken back: the boy belongs to Yahweh "all the days that he lives". Hannah asked Yahweh for him, and now she gives him to Yahweh as one "asked", sha'ul, a word that sounds like the name Saul.

decisions.choice: I in turn: Hannah answers Yahweh's gift with her own
decisions.reason: "And also I" sets Hannah's act beside Yahweh's: he gave her what she asked (verse 27), and she in turn gives the boy to him.

decisions.choice: he worshiped there: Elkanah, or the boy Samuel
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, "he bowed down". It may refer to Elkanah, the head of the family, or to the young Samuel, whose life before Yahweh begins here. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Latin translation read "they worshiped".

decisions.choice: granted (Literal); give, given over (Balanced); giving, belong (Readable)
decisions.reason: Familiar English versions say "lent", which keeps the repeated word but suggests a loan to be returned. Literal says "granted" twice, which keeps the repeated word with the right sense; Balanced and Readable say what the verb means (m1).

decisions.choice: "cédé" (Literal); "donne", "remis" (Balanced); "donne", "appartiendra" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on "asked" (verses 20, 27): what Hannah asked of the LORD she now hands over to him (m1). French has no verb that is both "ask" and "lend", so the levels follow the English choices; "prêté", the old rendering, would suggest the gift was only for a time, against "all the days that he lives".

decisions.choice: "cedido" (L); "entrego", "entregado" (B); "entrego", "pertenecerá" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English decision: "prestado" (lent) would suggest a loan to be returned, while Hannah gives Samuel for life (m1). Literal repeats one verb, "ceder", for the repeated Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: "người" for "he" who worshiped
decisions.reason: The subject may be Elkanah or the boy (meaning decision); "người" leaves it open, as the English "he" does.
